_doc: Revert-verify mutant for the READER half of the caller class in issue #4469 / req 2d072437-c19d-49a4-ae89-f20b6185571f. `get-body` found the end of the frontmatter block by the LENGTH of a hand-rebuilt `---\n<body>\n---`; that length equals the real one only for an LF file with no BOM, so widening `parse()` turned a fail-loud refusal (rc=1 on main 17.7.14) into a silent print of the file's own closing fence as body. MG1 restores exactly that arithmetic. Expectation written BEFORE the run.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/cli/src/commands/get-body.ts

MG1_slice_by_the_reconstructed_length._note: The pre-#4469 arithmetic. ⛔ CH60 (lone-CR) does NOT redden here, and the first edition of this spec expected it to — the expectation was derived from the mutant's THEME rather than from the arithmetic (integration-test-revert-verify §A44). Measured on the actual fixture: a lone-CR block's reconstruction is 44 chars and its real end is 44, because `\r` and `\n` are ONE character each — the length-slice lands correctly. Only CRLF (45 vs 47) and a BOM run shift it. What broke lone-CR before the fix was the SEPARATOR strip, which is MG2's business and which CH60 does redden. CH63 (pure LF, and a file ending at the closing fence) stays green for the same arithmetic reason, which is exactly why the defect stayed invisible until the predicate was widened.

MG2_separator_strip_back_to_lf_only._note: The block end is then correct but the ONE separator after the closing fence is only stripped for LF/CRLF, so a lone-CR file keeps a leading `\r` on its body. CH61/CH62 stay green (their separators are CRLF and LF) — the two halves of 'where does the body begin' are separate guarantees.
